$comment: GENERATED FILE. Do not edit.
Rebuild with spec/tools/Build-FogApiSpec.ps1 after changing either input.
Inputs: spec/openapi/fog-1.6.json (regenerated from fogproject) and
spec/overlay/fog-api-overlay.json (hand-maintained decisions).
Every emitter -- PowerShell, Python, bash -- reads this file and nothing else.

paging.description: maxRows is the row cap applied to a list request that does not carry a start parameter, that asks for length=-1, or that sends a negative length. A request with an explicit non-negative start and a positive length is served verbatim and is not capped, so a client that always pages explicitly never meets maxRows. expandMaxItems is different: an ?expand request has its page size clamped to this value even when a larger length was asked for, so a page can come back smaller than requested. Advance by the number of rows actually returned rather than by the length you asked for, and follow nextUrl until it is null.

security.note: Both tokens are already base64 as issued by the web UI. Send them verbatim; encoding them again double-encodes and 401s every call.

Every generated cmdlet must work against both, so the emitter reads this to
decide what to branch on.
fifteen.envelope: {count, <classname>s[]} rather than 1.6's DataTables-style envelope. Add-FogResultData already normalises this.

routeSpellings.$comment: 1.6 documents PUT /{class}/{id} and DELETE /{class}/{id}; 1.5 serves only the /edit and /delete spellings. 1.6 accepts both, so the /edit spelling is the one that works on both and is what the emitter uses.

fifteen.paging: None. No limit(), no complex(), no MAX_ROWS, no paginate. The query string is ignored and lists are unbounded, so the pager collapses to one request.

absentClasses.$comment: Classes in the 1.6 snapshot that 1.5 has no route for. A generated cmdlet for one of these has to fail clearly on 1.5 rather than 404 obscurely.

$comment: The functions that stay hand-written forever, and why. They are registered
rather than generated so the coverage matrix shows them as covered instead of
as gaps, and so the Python and bash emitters know which ones they owe.
category:
transport      the single HTTP choke point
l1             the generic CRUD layer everything else routes through
workflow       version branching, join-table reconciliation, multi-call
orchestration. Generating these would mean generating
judgement.
local          talks to the machine it runs on, not to FOG
utility        pure local logic, no API call
config         reads or writes the settings file
platform: any | windows | posix
targets: which emitters owe an equivalent

Send-FogWolTask.note: WOL is not a route: it is task with wol true / taskTypeID 14.

Get-FogHost.note: Identifies the local machine when given no parameters. The pure by-id read is what the generated Get-FogHost would be, which is why this one keeps the name and the generator skips host/indiv.

Repair-FogSnapinAssociations.note: FOG enforces no integrity on association rows; this reconciles them.

Get-FogVersion.note: Probes system/info then falls back to service/getversion.php for 1.5.

Get-FogInventory.note: Splits in phase 5.5 into Get-FogLocalInventory and Get-FogHostInventory.

$comment: Existing one-line wrappers over L1 that the generator would otherwise emit a
duplicate of. The generated name wins where they differ, and the existing name
becomes an alias -- never the reverse, and nothing here is deleted.
operation is the snapshot operationId these stand in for, so the coverage
matrix can mark it covered.
Operations that become a parameter on another cmdlet rather than a cmdlet of
their own. Emitting all 554 operations would produce a module nobody can
tab-complete through, and count/names/ids are modifiers on 'list' rather than
distinct things an admin wants to do.
join was folded onto New-Fog{Noun} -Upsert here, on the strength of the
document calling it an upsert against the natural key. That was wrong, and it
was caught by trying it against a real server: PUT /{class}/join is a BULK
EDIT over an explicit ids array, and sending it a body with no ids answers 202
and changes nothing. The upsert-by-name is the POST variant, and it exists on
group alone -- every other class answers 400.
Both are now described correctly upstream (fogproject openapi.class.php), so
the snapshot no longer misleads. Modelling them in FogApi is deferred rather
than guessed at, because neither fits the shape it was folded into: a bulk
edit is a plural cmdlet taking many ids, and a group-only get-or-create is a
hand-written group helper, not a generic per-class shape.

join.reason: PUT is a bulk edit over an ids array; POST is a group-only get-or-create. Neither is a modifier on an existing cmdlet, and both want their own design. Reachable meanwhile through Update-FogObject -uri.
join.putSemantics: PUT /{class}/join with {ids:[...], <fields>} applies those field values to every listed object, leaving omitted fields alone. 202, no body. No ids means no effect.
join.postSemantics: POST /group/join with {names:[...]} returns an id per name, creating any that do not exist. 201. Group only; all other classes answer 400.
